correctness.rationale: Re-audit of the replacement: parity gives precisely two minimizing deck candidates, with independent horizontal costs S,S' because the sum/difference map is onto and pushes product Haar to product Haar. Folding the triangular vertical-separation density gives a uniform z on [0,b/2]. The iid costs can be relabelled by the shorter vertical route, and J=b(b−2z) is independent uniform on [0,b²]. The coupled gain is (S−S'−J)_+, positive on an event of positive measure; this implies ordered tails and strictly smaller positive moments, not strict tail inequality at every threshold. The CDFs agree through b/2. Integrating in J, the gain equals (Var(S)−E[(S−S'−b²)_+²])/(2b²); Var(S)=Σa_i⁴/180. The essential supremum of S−S' is exactly Q, proving both directions of the cutoff including equality. The positive part of the sum is bounded by the sum of coordinate positive parts; each expectation is (a_i/2)²/6, half the corresponding horizontal second moment. The positive vertical second moment forces the strict lower ratio bound. Sharpness at every fixed k≥2 holds by taking a_1=2, all other periods and b tending to zero as specified in the replacement, so E[D_T²]→1/3 and the bounded gain integrand tends to one with expectation 1/6. Keeping horizontal periods fixed and sending b→∞ proves upper-endpoint sharpness. For the original ordinary formula, direct integration over the second horizontal cost gives (8/(15A²))∫_b^A(u²−b²)^(5/2)du, A=a/2. Rescaling gives the stated I(c); substituting u=c+(1−c)v gives a positive smooth coefficient times (1−c)^(7/2), with nonzero leading coefficient, verifying the stated transition. That ordinary formula is no longer a finding of the replacement.
residual_risks: Deterministic ordinary-bottle quadrature is corroborative only. The narrowed all-dimensional statements use the analytic proof, not finite tests or ordinary-limit extrapolation.

value.rationale: The repaired claim identifies exactly when horizontal opportunities for a shorter route are completely captured by a simple variance expression, in a natural class of compact flat metric-measure spaces. The dimension-independent ratio quantifies how far full-law shortening can go and is sharp even at fixed higher dimension. Those conclusions address a joint geometric effect, not a restatement of the ordinary-bottle integral.
residual_risks: No results are implied for arbitrary flat quotients, other deck actions, conditional distances or exact higher-moment cutoffs.
